column1: # Managed users: the single registry read by apply-system.sh (section `users`), the `usr` command, the SUPER+SHIFT+T picker
# and doctor.sh. Tab separated, `#` comments. Names, roles and colours only: never a secret, a password or an e-mail.
# The main user (the owner who runs apply-system.sh) is never listed here; the owner has full access to every managed home.
#   user     account name; must not be root or the owner
#   profile  dotfiles profile linked from /srv/dotfiles (profiles/<name>.txt), `-` = none
#   flags    comma separated:
#              service     background account: no terminal, not in the picker, no shared dotfiles (profile must be `-`)
#              noacl       the owner gets NO ACL on this home (default: u:OWNER:rwx + default ACL)
#              nobecome    no passwordless `sudo -u` and no passwordless `machinectl shell` for the owner (default: both)
#              clipboard   the user may write into the owner's Wayland clipboard (ACL on the Wayland socket only)
#              wayland     the user may open windows on the owner's Wayland socket (the same ACL: x on the runtime directory,
#                          rw on the socket, every other socket closed); a service user shows a popup that way (tgconfirm)
#              create      apply-system.sh creates the account when it does not exist (shell /usr/bin/nologin, password
#                          locked, home 0700); existing accounts (td, yc) are never created, re-shelled or re-grouped
#              interactive accepted for readability, it is the default for every non-service user
#   accent   palette token of the user's colour (themes/palette/everforest.json `shared`): tmux status and zsh prompt marker
#   note     free text
# Nothing else about a user is changed here: passwords, shells and groups (wheel, docker) of existing users stay as they are.
# Every managed user, whatever the flags, has NO access to the owner's home (the owner's ACL entries for it are removed).
# user
td
